en.title: Minimum Number of Range Increments
en.description:
Initially there is an all-zero array of length n. In one operation you can choose a non-empty contiguous subarray and increase all of its elements by 1 at the same time. Given a non-negative target array arr, find the minimum number of operations needed to turn the array into the target array.

This problem uses a standard input/output format compiled by CSWork; the algorithm rules follow the source problem, and the examples and test data were written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n (1 ≤ n ≤ 100000); the second line contains n integers arr[i] (0 ≤ arr[i] ≤ 10⁹). The answer may exceed the 32-bit integer range.
en.explanation: Example 1 starts 2 new operations at position 0 and another 2 at position 3, for 4 in total.
hints: The first position needs arr[0] operations. A later position needs to start arr[i]−arr[i−1] new operations only when it is higher than the previous position. Add up all the positive increments.
